title: AI papers in the 2026-10-23 arXiv announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This inferred ranking uses available independent discovery/curation signals, cross-category relevance, and reported evaluation evidence; citation evidence for this very recent batch is limited, so no citation totals or velocity are asserted.

sections.title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
sections.abstract: The authors introduce an executable benchmark that tests whether tool-using LLM agents seek omitted safety-relevant facts and distinguish prohibited from permissible actions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose EpiSEM-Bench and an independent audit procedure to measure unsafe execution under missing evidence and whether agents recover facts before acting.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported benchmark evidence covers ten evaluated model deployments and its six constructed domains; it does not establish failure rates in every real-world tool environment.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Featured in the Daily Agent Benchmarks index and Agentic Design's research feed; it spans two core AI categories and reports 300 matched task pairs across six domains and ten models.

sections.title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
sections.abstract: The paper proposes choosing partial reasoning rollouts by estimated pass@$k$, aiming to balance candidate quality and diversity while reducing the cost of completing many solutions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors formulate rollout selection as pass@$k$ optimization and derive a tractable submodular approximation with a greedy selection procedure; their experiments report gains over the compared pruning baselines, especially at moderate retained pool sizes.
sections.unique_caveat: The results depend on the learned representation of partial rollouts; the authors identify improving its correctness signal as future work.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in AI and language; it compares its pruning objective with both quality-based and diversity-based strategies across eight open-weight reasoning models, giving unusually direct evaluation coverage for this batch.

sections.title: AgenticEvolve: Evolutionary Program Search with Persistent Language Model Agents that Design and Run Experiments
sections.abstract: The authors embed persistent LLM agents in evolutionary program search so each agent can design and run experiments between candidate evaluations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that enabling the agent to experiment improves on an otherwise matched no-analysis configuration and existing baselines on their tested heuristic and equation-discovery tasks.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that execution uses protocol-level access restrictions but no operating-system sandbox; evaluation also covers a limited set of heuristic and equation-discovery tasks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across three core categories; the paper reports controlled comparisons on two heuristic-design tasks with three LLMs and twelve equation-discovery problems, and says source code is available.

sections.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
sections.abstract: The paper proposes a training-free metric for measuring alignment between a model's sensory representations and physical-motion structure, reporting positive correlation with robot-task success across evaluated embodied model families.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors define Sensorimotor Alignment (S²) as an offline proxy intended to prioritize models before closed-loop robot evaluation.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported result is correlational; the abstract does not establish that the metric predicts performance in new robot families or deployment settings.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The three-way cross-list connects vision, learning, and robotics; the authors provide a project/code page, and the abstract reports correlation across embodied model families plus a proposed use for screening VLM backbones before costly fine-tuning.

sections.title: Beyond Watching and Searching: Benchmarking Agents for Video-centered Deep Research Reports
sections.abstract: The authors define video-centered deep-research reporting and introduce a benchmark that tests whether agents can combine a source video with external multimodal evidence in an interactive, citation-linked report.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce OmniDR-Bench and Omni Atomic Rubric Trees for evaluating audiovisual grounding, multimodal evidence use, and report presentation; the best tested configuration scores 63.3/100.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors explicitly note remaining gaps in content coverage, cross-modal causal/logical analysis, and citation accuracy; the benchmark currently contains 50 tasks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in vision and language; the released OmniDR-Bench covers 50 bilingual tasks, 19 subcategories, and 18 agent configurations, and has an associated project repository.

sections.title: OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies
sections.abstract: The authors propose approximating unread attention-cache tails with count-aware proxy tokens, reporting retained accuracy and faster decoding at very low key-value-cache read rates.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine query-geometry clustering and selection with an error-gated, count-aware tail proxy; they report 99% of dense accuracy at 1% read for Llama-3.1-8B on RULER-32K HARD and a 10× faster decode-attention stage for their custom kernel.
sections.unique_caveat: The headline 99% figure is tied to a named benchmark/model setting, and the speed result uses the authors' custom kernel; neither alone establishes the same gains across hardware and production workloads.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It was picked up by an independent arXivDaily industry-trends digest; it is cross-listed in learning and AI and reports a concrete 1%-read result on RULER-32K HARD plus a custom-kernel speed comparison.

sections.title: RIDAR: Safeguarding Research Integrity in Autonomous Research Agents via Automated Detection and Runtime Intervention
sections.abstract: The authors present a taxonomy and system for detecting research-integrity violations in agent trajectories and intervening during execution, reporting detection and intervention results on three trajectory collections.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce a 14-type violation taxonomy and report that RIDAR-runtime reduces remaining violations by 36.8% in their 60 paired intervention trajectories.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that judgments may vary by LLM and trajectory, human review remains necessary in high-stakes settings, and their evaluation is mainly in mathematics and machine learning rather than specialized research-agent frameworks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper reports 85.2% F1 on 60 expert-annotated trajectories, analyzes 300 trajectories, and compares paired runtime-intervention runs; its arXiv page links to the project and code/data release.

sections.title: When Is a Memory Safe Enough to Act On? Action-Conditioned Verification for Long-Lived Agents
sections.abstract: The authors frame memory checking as an action-conditioned decision problem and propose a gate that chooses when to verify remembered premises, proceed, or abstain based on consequence, risk, and verification cost.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors formulate verification as a sequential stopping/bounded-value-of-information problem and report AMV-Guard's ToolSandbox and AppWorld results against a static policy.
sections.unique_caveat: The AppWorld transfer carries over the decision core but not the full structured pipeline and comes with a small reduction in safe-proceed recall and task success.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The work has been independently summarized by multiple AI-research outlets; it reports a 33.9% lower mean verification cost on ToolSandbox and a transfer test on AppWorld, making the operational trade-off measurable.

sections.title: Is Complex Agentic Memory Always Needed? Naive RAG Is Stronger Than We Thought
sections.abstract: The paper compares raw-history dense retrieval and reranking with more elaborate agentic memory systems, reporting that the simple baseline ranks first in six of seven tested benchmark-model settings.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that raw-history retrieval's greater evidence coverage can offset its lower utilization and recommend it as an essential baseline for the evaluated conversation-memory tasks.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is limited to the four evaluated conversation-memory benchmarks and their tested systems; it does not show that simple RAG is preferable for every persistent-memory or action-taking agent.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors test four memory benchmarks and seven benchmark-model settings, including comparisons with agentic memory systems; the result directly challenges a common design assumption and supplies a simple baseline for follow-up work.

sections.title: What Lies Beyond Perception: A Partition Theory of the Limits of AI Evaluation and Oversight
sections.abstract: The paper develops a formal account of how an evaluator's perceptual limits bound what behavioral tests can certify about a model, including whether it lacks a capability.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author proves a one-sided bound on evaluator-based certification and argues that behavioral evaluation alone cannot establish capability absence without assuming model cooperation.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is conditional on the evaluator's discrimination and the paper's stated acceptable-reply assumptions; it is not itself an empirical measurement of current deployed models.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across AI, machine learning, and computers-and-society; it supplies formal results and testable predictions directly relevant to interpreting benchmark and oversight claims, though independent attention evidence is sparse.
